text: Explain the types of sentence which are available to a judge when sentencing a young offender.
Assess which of these types of sentence might be most appropriate to encourage the offender to
rehabilitate. [25]
Describe how Parliament creates Acts of Parliament. Assess the advantages and disadvantages
of this method of law-making. [25]
Explain the role of the jury in both civil and criminal cases. Assess the extent to which jurors may
be influenced by their personal feelings or opinions. [25]
Explain the most common equitable maxims and remedies. Assess whether they are still relevant
to society today. [25]
Describe the composition of the Judicial Appointments Commission (JAC) and its role in selecting
inferior judges. Assess whether the JAC ensures that the best candidates are selected. [25]
After charge, but before trial, an individual can be remanded on bail by the court.
Explain how a court makes this decision and what conditions might be imposed. Assess the extent
to which the granting of bail to an individual charged with a crime imposes risks on society. [25]
